source_caption:
In The Wolf of Wall Street, the hilarious conversation where Jordan Belfort complains to his father, “Mad Max,” that he wants to “stay married” but the women throwing themselves at him are “all shaved,” was entirely improvised on the spot. Director Martin Scorsese deliberately cultivated a loose, collaborative “playground” atmosphere on set, encouraging his actors to freely ad-lib to capture the genuine, chaotic energy of the Stratton Oakmont brokers.
Veteran filmmaker and actor Rob Reiner—who hadn’t taken a major acting role in years and initially joked to Scorsese, “What’s more unbelievable? That he’s a Jew or that I am [Leonardo DiCaprio’s] father?”—stepped into the scene and perfectly matched DiCaprio’s increasingly ridiculous, off-the-cuff complaints. Reiner’s stunned, genuinely disgusted reactions (“Are you kidding me?!”) to Jordan’s wildly inappropriate oversharing were completely organic, resulting in one of the film’s funniest and most bizarrely candid father-son dynamics.

The Wolf of Wall Street (2013), directed by Martin Scorsese, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Jonah Hill, Margot Robbie, Matthew McConaughey, Rob Reiner. Based on the true story of Jordan Belfort, the film chronicles his rapid rise from an ambitious young stockbroker to a wildly wealthy, hedonistic titan of Wall Street, and his inevitable, spectacular fall brought on by rampant corruption, fraud, and drug addiction.

source_details.synopsis: The Wolf of Wall Street is a 2013 American biographical film co-produced and directed by Martin Scorsese, written by Terence Winter, and based on Jordan Belfort's 2007 memoir. It loosely recounts Belfort's career as a stockbroker in New York City and how his firm, Stratton Oakmont, engaged in rampant corruption and fraud on Wall Street, leading to his downfall. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort; Jonah Hill as his business partner and friend Donnie Azoff; Margot Robbie as his second wife, Naomi Lapaglia; Matthew McConaughey as his mentor and former boss Mark Hanna; and Kyle Chandler as FBI special agent Patrick Denham portraying Gregory Coleman.
